parole.significato: a common ending for many infinitive verbs
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech -ati, from Proto-Slavic *-ati.

parole.significato: appended to nouns to form an agent noun; used only on composite nouns expressing fields of knowledge
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech -ec, from Proto-Slavic *-ьcь.
Inherited from Old Czech -ina, from Proto-Slavic *-ina.

parole.significato: appended to words to create a feminine version of a noun, especially a profession, origin, or proper name
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ъka.
Inherited from Old Czech -ný, from Proto-Slavic *-ьnъ.

parole.significato: -ness: from adjectives, forms nouns indicating a property
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech -ost. Compare Old Church Slavonic -ость (-ostĭ).
Inherited from Old Czech -ský, from Proto-Slavic *-ьskъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *-iškas, from Proto-Indo-European *-iskos.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-ikъ.
Inherited from Old Czech a, from Proto-Slavic *a, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ō.

parole.significato: to be awake, not to be asleep
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech bdieti, from Proto-Slavic *bъděti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *budḗˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewdʰ- (“to (be) awake”), cognate with Serbo-Croatian bdeti.
Inherited from Old Czech blcha, from Proto-Slavic *blъxa, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *blúšāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰlúseh₂.
Inherited from Old Czech bledý.
Inherited from Old Czech blud, from Proto-Slavic *blǫdъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *blandás, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰlendʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech bobr, from Proto-Slavic *bobrъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *bebrus, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰébʰrus.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bodati, from earlier *bodìti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *bádīˀtei. Displaced Old Czech bósti, from which today archaic bůst.
Inherited from Old Czech brada, from Proto-Slavic *bordà, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *bardā́ˀ.
Inherited from Old Czech buditi, from Proto-Slavic *buditi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *báudīˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰowdʰéyeti, causative of *bʰewdʰ-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bydlò. By surface analysis, být + -dlo.

parole.significato: to be afraid of, to fear
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech báti.
Inherited from Old Czech býti, from Proto-Slavic *byti.
Inherited from Old Czech běžěti, from Proto-Slavic *běžati, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *bēˀgjā́ˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰégʷ-y-eh₂-ti, from *bʰegʷ-.
Inherited from Old Czech břieza, from Proto-Slavic *berza, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *berźas, *berźā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerHǵós, *bʰerHǵeh₂.
Inherited from Old Czech cělý, from Proto-Slavic *cělъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *káilas.
Inherited from Old Czech cěna, from Proto-Slavic *cěna, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kainā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷoynéh₂.
Inherited from Old Czech chrabrý, from Proto-Slavic *xorbrъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *skárˀbas, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kerb-.

parole.significato: strange, unfamiliar (not yet part of one's experience)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech cuzí.
Inherited from Old Czech dan, from Proto-Slavic *danь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dṓˀnis, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃-.
Inherited from Old Czech dci, from Proto-Slavic *dъ̏ťi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *duktḗ, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰugh₂tḗr, possibly from *dʰewgʰ- + *-tḗr.
Inherited from Old Czech dehet, from Proto-Slavic *degъtь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *degut(j)as, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech desět, from Proto-Slavic *desętь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *déśimt, from Proto-Indo-European *déḱm̥t.
Inherited from Old Czech devět, from Proto-Slavic *devętь.
Inherited from Old Czech dláto, from Proto-Slavic *dolto, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dálbtan, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰelbʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech dobrý, from Proto-Slavic *dobrъ. By surface analysis, doba + -rý.
Inherited from Old Czech drahý, from Proto-Slavic *dorgъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dargás, from Proto-Indo-European *dor-, *der-.
Inherited from Old Czech drozd, from Proto-Slavic *drozdъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *trasdás, from Proto-Indo-European *trósdos.
Inherited from Old Czech druh, from Proto-Slavic *drugъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *draugás, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰrewgʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech duch, from Proto-Slavic *dȗxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dáuṣas, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰows-o-s, from the root *dʰwes- (“to breathe, breath, spirit”).
Inherited from Old Czech dušě, from Proto-Slavic *duša.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dužь. By surface analysis, duh + -í.
Inherited from Old Czech dva, from Proto-Slavic *dъva, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *duwō, from Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dęsna.
Inherited from Old Czech dáti, from Proto-Slavic *dàti.
Inherited from Old Czech dým, from Proto-Slavic *dymъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dū́ˀmas, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰuh₂mós, from *dʰewh₂- + *-mós.
Inherited from Old Czech děd, from Proto-Slavic *dědъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dělo.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫsъ.

parole.significato: smooth (having a texture that lacks friction)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech hladký, from Proto-Slavic *gladъkъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *glā́ˀdus.
Inherited from Old Czech hlava, from Proto-Slavic *golvà.
Inherited from Old Czech hlína, from Proto-Slavic *glina, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gléiˀnāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *gleh₁y-.
Inherited from Old Czech hniezdo, from Proto-Slavic *gnězdo.
From Old Czech hon, from Proto-Slavic *gonъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gánas, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰónos.
Inherited from Old Czech hora, from Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH-.
Inherited from Old Czech hořěti, from Proto-Slavic *gorěti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garḗˀtei.
Inherited from Old Czech jhra, from Proto-Slavic *jьgra, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ígrāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ig-réh₂, from *h₂eyg-.
Inherited from Old Czech hrad, from Proto-Slavic *gȏrdъ.
Inherited from Old Czech hrdlo, from Proto-Slavic *gъrdlo, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gúrˀtlan, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷr̥h₃tlóm.
Inherited from Old Czech hřada, from Proto-Slavic *gręda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *grindā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrendʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech jahoda, from Proto-Slavic *agoda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ṓˀgāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ógeh₂.
Inherited from Old Czech jezero, from Proto-Slavic *ezero, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *éźeran.
Inherited from Old Czech jistiti, from jistý (“true, genuine”), from Proto-Slavic *jistъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ī́ˀstas, further origin uncertain.
Inherited from Old Czech jieti, from Proto-Slavic *ęti.
Inherited from Old Czech jiesti, from Proto-Slavic *ěsti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ēˀstei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁édti.
Inherited from Old Czech jíti, from Proto-Slavic *jьti.

Inherited from Old Czech kľúč, From Proto-Slavic *kľučь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kljaukjas, from Proto-Indo-European *klewk-yo-s, from *kle(h₂)uk-, an extended form of *(s)kleh₂w- (“hook, key, peg”).

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopьcь (“heap”), from *kopъ (see *kopa) + *-ьcь, akin to *kopati (“to dig”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kop-, probably from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kep- (“to strike, beat”).
Inherited from Old Czech krev, from Proto-Slavic *kry̑.

From Old Czech krušec (“lump of a useful mineral, especially rock salt”), krušek, from kruch (“piece, chunk”), from Proto-Slavic *kruxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kraušas, from Proto-Indo-European *krows-o-s, ultimately from *krews- (“to freeze, become hard”).

parole.significato: cow (female domesticated ox or other bovine, especially an adult after she has had a calf)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech kráva.

parole.significato: club, cudgel (a short heavy club with a rounded head used as a weapon)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kyjь.
Inherited from Old Czech kámen, from Proto-Slavic *kamy. The long ⟨á⟩ is probably from archaic Czech *kámy.

parole.significato: stake, post (pointed, long, slender piece of wood)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech kól, from Proto-Slavic *kolъ. Probably connected with *kolti (“to chop”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kálˀtei, originally from Proto-Indo-European *kel-.
Inherited from Old Czech kóra, from Proto-Slavic *kora.
Inherited from Old Czech led, from Proto-Slavic *ledъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ledús.
Inherited from Old Czech lehnúti, derived from Old Czech léci, from Proto-Slavic *leťi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *légtei, from Proto-Indo-European *légʰeti, from *legʰ-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *lemešь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *lémešis.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *letъ.
Inherited from Old Czech lúpiti, from Proto-Slavic *lupiti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *laupī́ˀtei.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ložiti.
Inherited from Old Czech luk, from Proto-Slavic *lǫkъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *lankás, from Proto-Indo-European *lenk- (“to bend”).

Inherited from Old Czech luna, from Proto-Slavic *lunà, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *láukšnāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *lówksneh₂. Cognates include Latin lūna, Ancient Greek λύχνος (lúkhnos), Old Prussian lauxnos and Middle Irish luan.

parole.significato: to lambaste, to scold (with na or the object in dative)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech láti, from Proto-Slavic *làjati, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *lā́ˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂-. Cognate with Polish łajać.

parole.significato: to please [with dative ‘someone’] (idiomatically translated by English like with subject and object reversed)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech ľúbiti, from Proto-Slavic *ľūbìti.
Inherited from Old Czech lécha, from Proto-Slavic *lěxa, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *láišāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *lóyseh₂, from *leys-.

parole.significato: lime, linden, basswood (a deciduous tree of the genus Tilia)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech lípa, from Proto-Slavic *lipa, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *léiˀpāˀ.
Inherited from Old Czech lýko, from Proto-Slavic *lyko, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *lúnˀkan. Cognate with Lower Sorbian łyko, Polish łyko, Serbo-Croatian lika, Russian лы́ко (lýko).
Inherited from Old Czech malý, from Proto-Slavic *màlъ.
Inherited from Old Czech milý, from Proto-Slavic *milъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *meiʔlos, from Proto-Indo-European *meyl-.

parole.significato: to grind (to make smaller by breaking with a device)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech mléti, from Proto-Slavic *melti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mélˀtei.
From Proto-Slavic *mъnogъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *managas, from Proto-Indo-European *monogʰos.
Inherited from Old Czech mieti, from Proto-Slavic *męti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mínˀtei. Compare Russian мять (mjatʹ).
Inherited from Old Czech modliti, from Proto-Slavic *modliti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *maldī́ˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *meldʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech múdrý, from Proto-Slavic *mǫdrъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *murъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mauˀras, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mewr-.

Inherited from Old Czech mozk, from Proto-Slavic *mozgъ (“marrow, brain”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *masgás, from Proto-Indo-European *mosgʰós. Cognate with Russian мозг (mozg, “marrow, brain”), English marrow
Inherited from Old Czech moře, from Proto-Slavic *moře.
Inherited from Old Czech muž, from Proto-Slavic *mǫžь.
Inherited from Old Czech myš, from Proto-Slavic *myšь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *mū́ˀšis, from Proto-Indo-European *múHs. The computing sense is a semantic loan from English mouse.
Inherited from Old Czech máti, from Proto-Slavic *mati.

parole.significato: measure (quantity, size, weight, distance or capacity of a substance compared to a designated standard)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech miera.
Inherited from Old Czech miesiti, from Proto-Slavic *měsiti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *máiśīˀtei.
Inherited from Old Czech nahý, from Proto-Slavic *nagъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nōˀgás, from Proto-Indo-European *nogʷós.
Inherited from Old Czech ne, from Proto-Slavic *ne.
Inherited from Old Czech nebe, nebo, from Proto-Slavic *nebo, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nébas, from Proto-Indo-European *nébʰos.
Inherited from Old Czech nit, from Proto-Slavic *nitь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *nī́ˀtis, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)neh₁-.
Inherited from Old Czech nos.
Inherited from Old Czech nový, from Proto-Slavic *nòvъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *náwas, from Proto-Indo-European *néwos.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *o(b), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ebʰi. See o.
Inherited from Old Czech obúti, from Proto-Slavic *obuti (“to put on (footwear)”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *outei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ew-. Cognate with Latin induere.
Inherited from Old Czech oheň, from Proto-Slavic *ogňь.
Inherited from Old Czech oko, from Proto-Slavic *oko.
Inherited from Old Czech ono.
Inherited from Old Czech orel, from Proto-Slavic *orьlъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *arélis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃érō.
Inherited from Old Czech ostrý, from Proto-Slavic *ostrъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *aśras, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱrós.
Inherited from Old Czech ovcě, from Proto-Slavic *ovьca, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *áwis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ówis.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *volděti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *walˀdā́ˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂welh₁dʰh₁-, from *h₂welh₁- (“to rule”).
Inherited from Old Czech padnúti, from former Old Czech pásti, from Proto-Slavic *pasti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pṓˀstei, from Proto-Indo-European *ped-.

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pizda, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pīˀsdāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *písdeh₂.
Inherited from Old Czech plch, from Proto-Slavic *pьlxъ, possibly from Proto-Balto-Slavic *peliā, from Proto-Indo-European *pelH-.
Inherited from Old Czech plný, from Proto-Slavic *pьlnъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pílˀnas, from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁nós.
Inherited from Old Czech plúti, from Proto-Slavic *pluti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pláuˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₃(w)-. Doublet of plovat.
From Old Czech po, from Proto-Slavic *po, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó.
Inherited from Old Czech po-.
Inherited from Old Czech pút, from Proto-Slavic *pǫtь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pántis, from Proto-Indo-European *póntoh₁s.
Inherited from Old Czech pro-, from Proto-Slavic *pro-.
Inherited from Old Czech prositi, from Proto-Slavic *prositi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *práśīˀtei.
Inherited from Old Czech prs, from Proto-Slavic *pьrsь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pírˀśis, from Proto-Indo-European *pérḱus.
Inherited from Old Czech prvý, from Proto-Slavic *pьrvъ.
Inherited from Old Czech psáti.

parole.significato: to prick, to stab, to poke
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech píchati, from Proto-Slavic *pьxàti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pištei, from Proto-Indo-European *pis-é-ti, from *peys- (“to crush”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *pěstъ.

parole.significato: whistle (device used to make a whistling sound)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech píščala, from Proto-Slavic *piščalь, from *piskati, *piščati (“to squeak, whistle”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pīṣk-. Doublet of pistole.
Inherited from Old Czech pěst, from Proto-Slavic *pęstь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *penkstis, from Proto-Indo-European *pn̥kʷstis, from *pewǵ-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *per-.
Inherited from Old Czech přěsný, from Proto-Slavic *prěsnъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *prḗˀskas.
Inherited from Old Czech rež, from Proto-Slavic *rъžь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *rugís, itself probably of substrate origin.

parole.significato: horn (a hard growth of keratin that protrudes from the top of the head of certain animals)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech roh, from Proto-Slavic *rogъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *rágas.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ruda.
Inherited from Old Czech ruka, from Proto-Slavic *rǫka, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ránkāˀ.

parole.significato: to sit (to be in a sitting position)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech sěděti, from Proto-Slavic *sěděti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sēdḗˀtei, from *sedéh₁yeti, from Proto-Indo-European *sed-.
Inherited from Old Czech siemě, from Proto-Slavic *sěmę, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sḗˀmin, from Proto-Indo-European *séh₁mn̥.
Inherited from Old Czech sen, from Proto-Slavic *sъ̀nъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *súpnas, from Proto-Indo-European *supnós.
Inherited from Old Czech sestra, from Proto-Slavic *sestra.
Inherited from Old Czech sladký, from Proto-Slavic *soldъkъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *salˀdus, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂l-.
Inherited from Old Czech sled, Proto-Slavic *slědъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sláidus.
Inherited from Old Czech slíva, from Proto-Slavic *sliva, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *slīˀwā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leh₃y-.

parole.significato: to stink (to have a strong bad smell)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech smrděti, from Proto-Slavic *smьrděti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *smirˀdḗˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)merd-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sȍkъ (“juice, sap”).
Inherited from Old Czech súkati, from Proto-Slavic *sukati.
From Old Czech sršen, from Proto-Slavic *sьrxy (stem *sьršen-), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *śirˀšṓ, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂s-. Cognate with Lithuanian širšė, Latin crābrō, English hornet.
Inherited from Old Czech sto, from Proto-Slavic *sъto, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *śímta, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm.
Inherited from Old Czech stroj, from Proto-Slavic *strojь.

parole.significato: middle, midpoint, center (point in the center of a two dimensional shape like a circle)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *serda.
Inherited from Old Czech suchý, from Proto-Slavic *suxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *saušás, from Proto-Indo-European *sh₂ewsos.
Inherited from Old Czech svatý, from Proto-Slavic *svętъ.
Inherited from Old Czech syn, from Proto-Slavic *sy̑nъ.
Inherited from Old Czech sám, from Proto-Slavic *samъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sāmas, from Proto-Indo-European *somHós.
Inherited from Old Czech sieti, from Proto-Slavic *sěti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sḗˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *séh₁-ye-ti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *syrъ.
Inherited from Old Czech tesati, from Proto-Slavic *tesati, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *téśtei.
Inherited from Old Czech tisúc, from Proto-Slavic *tysǫti, *tysęti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tūˀsantis, from Proto-Indo-European *tuHsont-, *tuHsenti-. Akin to English thousand.

Inherited from Old Czech tur, from Proto-Slavic *tȗrъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *taurás, from Proto-Indo-European *táwros.
Inherited from Old Czech tvrdý, from Proto-Slavic *tvьrdъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *twírˀtas, from Proto-Indo-European *twerH-.
Inherited from Old Czech ty, from Proto-Slavic *ty, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tūˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *túh₂.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tata.

parole.significato: to flow (to move as a fluid)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech téci, from Proto-Slavic *teťi, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tek-, from Proto-Indo-European *tekʷ- (“to run, flow”).
Inherited from Old Czech třie, tři, from Proto-Slavic *tri, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tríjes, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫglь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ánˀglis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óngʷl̥ (“charcoal”).Compare Serbo-Croatian ugalj.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *umъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫžь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ángis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éngʷʰis.
Inherited from Old Czech vařiti, from Proto-Slavic *variti.
Inherited from Old Czech vdova, from Proto-Slavic *vьdova, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁widʰéwh₂.
Inherited from Old Czech vajce, from Proto-Slavic *ājьcè, diminutive of *ȃje (“egg”), ultimately from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ṓjan (“egg”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”).
Inherited from Old Czech veselý, from Proto-Slavic *veselъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wéselas, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wésus.
Inherited from Old Czech vetchý, from Proto-Slavic *vetъxъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wétušas, from Proto-Indo-European *wet-.
Inherited from Old Czech večer, from Proto-Slavic *večerъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wékeras, from Proto-Indo-European *wekʷsperos. Compare Polish wieczór.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vidъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wéiˀdas, from Proto-Indo-European *wéydos, from *weyd-.
Inherited from Old Czech viděti, from Proto-Slavic *viděti.
Inherited from Old Czech vlast, from Proto-Slavic *volstь.
Inherited from Old Czech vlk, from Proto-Slavic *vьlkъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wilkás, from Proto-Indo-European *wĺ̥kʷos.
Inherited from Old Czech vlna, from Proto-Slavic *vьlna (“wave”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wiln-, from Proto-Indo-European *wl̥Hn-.
Inherited from Old Czech vládnúti, from Proto-Slavic *volsti.
Inherited from Old Czech voda, from Proto-Slavic *voda.
Inherited from Old Czech voditi, from Proto-Slavic *vodìti.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *voliti.

parole.significato: one of threads of hair which form a beard
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ǫsъ.
Inherited from Old Czech voziti, from Proto-Slavic *voziti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wáźīˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *woǵʰéyeti, from *weǵʰ-.

Inherited from Old Czech vrah (“enemy, murderer”), from Proto-Slavic *vorgъ (“foe, enemy”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wargás (“foe, enemy”). Cognates include Russian враг (vrag, “enemy”), a false friend.
Inherited from Old Czech vrána, from Proto-Slavic *vorna, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wárˀnāˀ.
Inherited from Old Czech vrátiti, from Proto-Slavic *vortiti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wártīˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *wortéyeti, from the root *wert-.

parole.significato: a prefix, often indicating the perfective aspect
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech vy-, from Proto-Slavic *vy-. Doublet of vý-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vydra, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ūdrāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *udréh₂, the feminine form of *udrós. Doublet of hydra.
Inherited from Old Czech vésti, from Proto-Slavic *vesti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *westéi, from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰ-.

parole.significato: to twine, to wind, to weave, to plait
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech víti, from Proto-Slavic *vī́tī, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wīˀtei, from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁y-. Cognate with Polish wić, Russian вить (vitʹ), Serbo-Croatian vȉti.

Inherited from Old Czech včera, from Proto-Slavic *vьčerà. By surface analysis, from večer (“evening”) (possibly a remnant of the original instrumental suffix as reconstructed in Proto-Balto-Slavic *wékerōˀ, compare doma).
Inherited from Old Czech věděti, from Proto-Slavic *věděti.
Inherited from Old Czech věnec, from Proto-Slavic *věnьcь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *waiˀníkas, from Proto-Indo-European *woyh₁níkos.
Inherited from Old Czech vóz, from Proto-Slavic *vozъ.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zemь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źem- (“ground”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéǵʰōm. Compare země which comes from Proto-Slavic *zemľa.
Inherited from Old Czech země, from Proto-Slavic *zemľa.
Inherited from Old Czech zima, from Proto-Slavic *zima, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źeimā́ˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéyōm.
Inherited from Old Czech zlato, from Proto-Slavic *zolto.
Inherited from Old Czech zlý, from Proto-Slavic *zъlъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źulas, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwel-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zmьja.
Inherited from Old Czech zúti, from Proto-Slavic *jьzuti (“to take off (footwear)”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *áutei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ew-. Cognate with Latin exuere.

parole.significato: grain (harvested seeds of various grass-related food crops)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech zrno, from Proto-Slavic *zьrno, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źírˀnan, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵr̥h₂nóm.

parole.significato: tooth (structure present in the mouth of many animals)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech zub, from Proto-Slavic *zǫbъ.
Inherited from Old Czech črný, from Proto-Slavic *čьrnъ.
Inherited from Old Czech črv, from Proto-Slavic *čьrvь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kírmis, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷŕ̥mis.
Inherited from Old Czech česati, from Proto-Slavic *česati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *černъ.
Inherited from Old Czech čtyřie, čtyři, from Proto-Slavic *četyre, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ketū́res, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwóres.

parole.significato: to cut (to perform an incision, for example with a knife)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Czech řězati, from Proto-Slavic *rězati, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *rḗˀźtei, from Proto-Indo-European *wreh₁ǵ-.
Inherited from Old Czech ščít, from Proto-Slavic *ščitъ (“shield”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *skeitum, *skoitum, from Proto-Indo-European *skey-to-m, from *skey- (“to cut, separate”).
Inherited from Old Czech želud, from Proto-Slavic *želǫdь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gel-, *gil-, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷelh₂-.
Inherited from Old Czech řebro, from Proto-Slavic *rebrò, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *rébran, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rebʰróm, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rebʰ-.
Inherited from Old Czech žena, from Proto-Slavic *žena.
Inherited from Old Czech žrnov, from Proto-Slavic *žьrny, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gírˀnūˀs, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷréh₂wō.
Inherited from Old Czech žéci, from Proto-Slavic *žeťi, from earlier *gegti, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *degtéi, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰégʷʰeti, from *dʰegʷʰ-.

parole.significato: rye, any member of the genus Secale
parole.testo: From Old Czech žito, from Proto-Slavic *žito (“grain, corn”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *géiˀtan, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷéyh₃tom. First attested in the 14th century.
Inherited from Old Czech živý, from Proto-Slavic *živъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gīˀwas, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷih₃wós (“alive”).
Inherited from Old Czech žádati.
